stops.note: Set apart by the Holy Spirit and sent out by the church at Antioch
Sailed for Cyprus from Antioch's port
Proclaimed the word in the Jewish synagogues
Confronted the sorcerer Elymas before the proconsul
John Mark left the team here and returned to Jerusalem
Preached in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch; the message turned to the Gentiles
A great number of Jews and Greeks believed
Healed a man lame from birth; stoned and left for dead
Made many disciples — the farthest point of the journey, then retraced their steps through Lystra, Iconium, and Pisidian Antioch, appointing elders in each church
Sailed for home from this port
Reported all God had done, and that He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles
Set out with Silas, commended by the church to the grace of the Lord
Strengthened the churches of Paul's home region, Cilicia
Revisited the disciples
Timothy joined the team here
A vision of a man of Macedonia pleading, "Come over and help us"
First landfall in Europe
Lydia converted; Paul and Silas imprisoned, then freed by an earthquake
Passed through on the Via Egnatia
Passed through toward Thessalonica
Reasoned in the synagogue from the Scriptures for three Sabbaths
The Bereans examined the Scriptures daily to test what Paul taught
Addressed the Areopagus on the altar "to an unknown god"
Stayed eighteen months; met Priscilla and Aquila
Took a vow and had his hair cut before sailing for Syria
A brief stop — reasoned with the Jews there before sailing on
Landed, then went up to greet the church
Returned to the church that had sent him out
Set out again through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening every disciple
Stayed nearly three years; a riot broke out among the silversmiths of Artemis
Three months in Greece
Kept the Days of Unleavened Bread here on the return
Raised Eutychus after he fell from a third-story window during Paul's long sermon
Walked here overland while the ship sailed around the cape
Farewell to the Ephesian elders: "you will not see my face again"
Disciples urged him, through the Spirit, not to go to Jerusalem
The prophet Agabus bound his own hands and feet, warning of Paul's arrest
Arrived, and was arrested in the temple soon after
Departed as a prisoner under guard, having appealed to Caesar
Allowed ashore to be cared for by friends
Transferred to an Alexandrian grain ship bound for Italy
Progress slowed by contrary winds
Paul warned the voyage would end in disaster; the centurion sailed on anyway
Shipwrecked on Malta after fourteen days adrift; survived a viper's bite
Three days ashore
Found believers here and stayed a week
Roman believers walked out from the city to meet him at the Forum of Appius
More believers met him here
Under house arrest for two years, he welcomed all who visited and taught boldly, unhindered
Set out on the night of the Passover, six hundred thousand men on foot besides women and children — the start of the Exodus
First camp after Rameses; a mixed multitude of non-Israelites went up with them
The LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind all night, and the people crossed on dry ground
Arrived in the third month; the LORD gave the Law and made His covenant with Israel here
The twelve spies returned here; Israel's unbelief at the report turned a short journey into forty years of wandering
Camped on the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho — where Moses would deliver Deuteronomy and die within sight of the promised land
Terah took Abram, his wife Sarai, and his grandson Lot from Ur of the Chaldeans, setting out for Canaan
Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran at the LORD's call, after Terah's death there
His first stop in Canaan, at the oak of Moreh — the LORD first promised him this land
Pitched his tent between Bethel and Ai, built an altar, and called on the name of the LORD
A famine drove him down to Egypt, where he passed Sarai off as his sister out of fear
Went up out of Egypt into the Negev, very rich in livestock, silver, and gold
Moved his tents to the oaks of Mamre at Hebron and built an altar there, where he would live for decades
Zedekiah and his soldiers fled the besieged city by night after the Babylonians broke through the wall
Captured near Jericho and brought here; Nebuchadnezzar had Zedekiah's sons killed before his eyes, then had him blinded
Taken to Babylon in bronze shackles — the exile Jeremiah had long foretold
Israel sent for the Ark of the Covenant from Shiloh, hoping it would save them from the Philistines
Israel's camp before the battle where the Philistines captured the Ark and thirty thousand fell
Brought to the temple of Dagon, whose idol was found fallen face-down before the Ark two mornings running
Moved here after Ashdod was struck with tumors — Gath suffered the same plague in turn
The Ekronites cried out in terror the moment it arrived, refusing to keep it any longer
Sent home on a new cart pulled by nursing cows; the reapers here rejoiced to see it return
Kept in Abinadab's house on the hill for twenty years, after the men of Beth-shemesh asked it be moved on
David finally brought it up with rejoicing and sacrifice, after Uzzah's death had halted the first attempt
Returned to His hometown and read from Isaiah in the synagogue; the crowd tried to throw Him off a cliff
Made this fishing town by the lake His ministry base after Nazareth rejected Him
Went throughout Galilee preaching in synagogues and driving out demons, town after town
Asked the disciples, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?" — Peter's confession, far north near the springs of the Jordan
Set His face to go to Jerusalem — the long final journey toward the cross
